Titel: Market Response Models: Econometric and Time Series Analysis
Autor / Quelle: Dominique M. Hanssens, Leonard J. Parsons, Randall L. Schultz, 2001, 2nd edition, Kluwer/Springer (International Series in Quantitative Marketing 12), book
Notiz: Still the reference text for aggregate response modelling: sales response functions, lag structures (Koyck and adstock), elasticities, time-series methods (persistence, VAR) and how response models feed allocation decisions. Dense but exact; most Google and Meta MMM papers cite it.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 reading (chapters on response model specification and lag structures) and session 3 (decision models and allocation). Paywalled; library copy or e-book, roughly EUR 150 to 200 new.

Titel: Modeling Markets: Analyzing Marketing Phenomena and Improving Marketing Decision Making
Autor / Quelle: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt, Koen H. Pauwels, 2015, Springer (International Series in Quantitative Marketing), book, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-2086-0 (verified via chapter link)
Notiz: The most teachable modern textbook on marketing models: specification, estimation, validation and use, with a full chapter of worked aggregate-demand models (chapter 7, "Examples of models for aggregate demand"). European authors, European examples.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 core reading (chapters on model building and aggregate demand), session 4 for validation chapters. WU library likely has Springer access; otherwise paywalled.

Autor / Quelle: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt, Koen H. Pauwels (eds), 2017, Springer, edited book, DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-53469-5 (verified)
Notiz: Companion volume with chapters on Bayesian analysis, time-series models, endogeneity, structural models and mixture models, each written by specialists. The Bayesian and endogeneity chapters are the academic bridge to Meridian and PyMC-Marketing.
Verwendung im Kurs: Background for session 2 (Bayesian chapter) and session 4 (endogeneity, time series). Paywalled; Springer access needed.

Titel: Python for Marketing Research and Analytics
Autor / Quelle: Jason S. Schwarz, Chris Chapman, Elea McDonnell Feit, 2020, Springer, textbook with code, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-49720-0 (verified); code at https://github.com/python-marketing-research/python-marketing-research-1ed (verified)
Notiz: The only mainstream marketing analytics textbook written in Python (pandas, statsmodels, scikit-learn), by two Google researchers and a Penn professor. Covers data handling, linear models, model interpretation and segmentation with marketing data; no MMM chapter, but it sets the coding baseline. The R twin is Chapman and Feit, R for Marketing Research and Analytics, 2nd ed., 2019, Springer, with f
Verwendung im Kurs: Pre-course or session 1 lab warm-up (chapters on data wrangling and linear models). Paywalled book; GitHub notebooks are free.

Autor / Quelle: Rob J. Hyndman, George Athanasopoulos, 2021, OTexts, open textbook (R; a Python edition is in progress at https://otexts.com/fpppy/ (unverified, site blocked here))
Notiz: Free, rigorous and readable; the standard text for the forecasting half of the course (decomposition, ETS, ARIMA, regression with ARIMA errors, hierarchical and grouped forecasting across countries and products).
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading (chapters on time series regression, ARIMA and hierarchical forecasting). Free.

Titel: Bayesian Modeling and Computation in Python
Autor / Quelle: Osvaldo A. Martin, Ravin Kumar, Junpeng Lao, 2021, Chapman and Hall/CRC, textbook, free online
Notiz: Written by PyMC and ArviZ core developers; covers priors, MCMC diagnostics, hierarchical models and time series in exactly the stack PyMC-Marketing uses. The practical companion for anyone fitting a Bayesian MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 background (chapters on Bayesian inference, hierarchical models, model comparison). Free online; print edition paywalled.

Titel: The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality
Autor / Quelle: Nick Huntington-Klein, 2022, Chapman and Hall/CRC, textbook, free online with R, Stata and Python code
Notiz: The friendliest serious causal-inference text; the chapters on difference-in-differences, synthetic control and event studies are exactly the toolkit behind geo experiments, GeoLift and CausalImpact.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading (difference-in-differences, synthetic control chapters) before the experiment lab. Free.

Titel: Causal Inference for the Brave and True
Autor / Quelle: Matheus Facure, 2022 onward, open online book in Python (the author's O'Reilly book Causal Inference in Python, 2023, is the paid version (unverified))
Notiz: Python-first, notebook-based treatment of potential outcomes, regression, DiD, synthetic control and uplift, written by a practitioner; students can run every chapter.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 lab companion (synthetic control and DiD chapters). Free.

Autor / Quelle: Scott Cunningham, 2021, Yale University Press, textbook, free online with R, Stata and Python code
Notiz: Clear, example-driven treatment of DAGs, matching, DiD and synthetic control; the DAG chapter is the best short preparation for Meridian's causal-graph framing of MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Background for session 4; assign the DAG and synthetic control chapters. Free online.

Titel: Effective Advertising: Understanding When, How, and Why Advertising Works
Autor / Quelle: Gerard J. Tellis, 2004, Sage, book
Notiz: Synthesises decades of econometric and experimental evidence on advertising response: elasticities, carryover, wear-in and wear-out, and the comparison of field experiments with econometric estimates. The qualitative counterpart to the elasticity meta-analyses.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 background (chapters on advertising carryover and market-level effects). Paywalled; a scanned copy is on the Internet Archive lending library.

Titel: Empirical Generalizations about Marketing Impact (2nd edition)
Autor / Quelle: Dominique M. Hanssens (ed.), 2015, Marketing Science Institute (Relevant Knowledge Series), book
Notiz: About 120 one-page empirical generalisations (advertising elasticity, price elasticity, carryover, long-term effects, cross-country patterns), each with references. Ideal for setting Bayesian priors and for sanity-checking student MMM output.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 (prior elicitation exercise) and session 3. Paid MSI publication (about USD 40 as e-book); short extracts are quotable.

Titel: Principles of Marketing Engineering and Analytics (3rd edition)
Autor / Quelle: Gary L. Lilien, Arvind Rangaswamy, Arnaud De Bruyn, 2017, DecisionPro, textbook with Excel tools (unverified)
Notiz: The classic "marketing engineering" treatment of response functions and resource allocation (ADBUDG-style curves, allocation across segments and regions) with managerial cases; useful to show the pre-Bayesian logic of budget optimisation.
Verwendung im Kurs: Background for session 3. Paywalled, with a student software licence.

Titel: Aggregate Advertising Models: The State of the Art
Autor / Quelle: John D. C. Little, 1979, Operations Research 27(4), 629 to 667, article
Notiz: The founding statement of what an advertising response model must capture: carryover, diminishing returns, competition, interaction and dynamics. Every adstock-plus-Hill MMM is a descendant.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 required reading (sections 1 to 4). Paywalled (INFORMS).

Titel: Econometric Measurement of the Duration of Advertising Effect on Sales
Autor / Quelle: Darral G. Clarke, 1976, Journal of Marketing Research 13(4), 345 to 357, article
Notiz: Shows that implied carryover depends heavily on the data interval (the data-interval bias), which is still the main reason weekly MMMs and annual studies disagree on decay rates.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 or 2 reading when introducing adstock decay. Paywalled (Sage/JSTOR).

Titel: The Persistence of Marketing Effects on Sales
Autor / Quelle: Marnik G. Dekimpe, Dominique M. Hanssens, 1995, Marketing Science 14(1), 1 to 21, article
Notiz: Introduces persistence modelling (unit roots, VAR, impulse responses) to separate short-run from long-run marketing effects; the methodological root of "long-term effects" claims in MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 background; session 4 for time-series thinking. Paywalled.

Titel: How Well Does Advertising Work? Generalizations from Meta-Analysis of Brand Advertising Elasticities
Autor / Quelle: Raj Sethuraman, Gerard J. Tellis, Richard A. Briesch, 2011, Journal of Marketing Research 48(3), 457 to 471, article
Notiz: Mean short-term advertising elasticity 0.12, long-term 0.24, with moderators (durables, life-cycle stage, data interval, GRPs versus money, Europe versus US). The best single source of priors for a Bayesian MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 required reading (use the moderator table to set priors). Paywalled, open PDF available.

Titel: A Meta-Analysis of Marketing Communication Carryover Effects
Autor / Quelle: Christine Köhler, Murali K. Mantrala, Sönke Albers, Vamsi K. Kanuri, 2017, Journal of Marketing Research 54(6), article
Notiz: Meta-analysis of carryover (decay) estimates across media and countries; gives defensible ranges for adstock parameters and shows how data interval and model type bias them.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 (adstock priors); pairs with Clarke 1976. Paywalled.

Autor / Quelle: Dominique M. Hanssens, Koen H. Pauwels, 2016, Journal of Marketing 80(6), 173 to 190, article
Notiz: Frames marketing accountability as a chain from spend to metrics to financial value and reviews what response models, attribution and experiments can and cannot show. A good opening reading for managers-in-training.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 reading. Paywalled, open PDF available.

Titel: How T.V. Advertising Works: A Meta-Analysis of 389 Real World Split Cable T.V. Advertising Experiments
Autor / Quelle: Leonard M. Lodish, Magid Abraham, Stuart Kalmenson, Jeanne Livelsberger, Beth Lubetkin, Bruce Richardson, Mary Ellen Stevens, 1995, Journal of Marketing Research 32(2), 125 to 139, article
Notiz: The classic experimental benchmark: about half of TV weight tests show no significant sales effect, and effects are larger for new products. Sets expectations before students see MMM ROI claims.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 background (experiments versus models). Paywalled.

Titel: Bayesian Methods for Media Mix Modeling with Carryover and Shape Effects
Autor / Quelle: Yuxue Jin, Yueqing Wang, Yunting Sun, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
Notiz: The canonical modern MMM specification: geometric or delayed adstock plus a Hill saturation curve, estimated with Bayesian methods, with ROAS and marginal ROAS derived from the posterior. LightweightMMM, PyMC-Marketing and Meridian all implement it.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 required reading; reproduce its simulated example in the PyMC-Marketing lab. Free.

Titel: Geo-level Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Modeling
Autor / Quelle: Yunting Sun, Yueqing Wang, Yuxue Jin, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
Notiz: Pooling sub-national (geo) data in a hierarchical model gives tighter credible intervals than national data alone. This is the statistical justification for the country-by-region hierarchies in Meridian and for multi-country MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 required reading (geo hierarchies across countries). Free.

Titel: Challenges and Opportunities in Media Mix Modeling
Autor / Quelle: David Chan, Michael Perry, 2017, Google research white paper
Notiz: Short, honest list of why MMM is hard: limited variation, collinearity, selection bias (ads follow demand), funnel effects, paid search, and the need for experiments. Excellent framing paper.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 or 2 reading; discussion piece. Free.

Titel: A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach to Improve Media Mix Models Using Category Data
Autor / Quelle: Yueqing Wang, Yuxue Jin, Yunting Sun, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
Notiz: Uses category-level data across brands as a hierarchical prior to stabilise a single brand's MMM; a practical answer to short series, and the same logic applies to pooling across countries.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 background. Free.

Titel: Introduction to the Aggregate Marketing System Simulator
Autor / Quelle: Stephanie Zhang, Jon Vaver, 2017, Google research white paper; R package https://github.com/google/amss (verified, archived 2022)
Notiz: A simulator that generates realistic aggregate marketing data with known ground-truth ROAS, so MMM methods can be tested. Ideal for teaching: students fit models to data where the true answer is known.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 or 4 lab (simulate, fit, compare to truth). Free, R.

Titel: Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Model Incorporating Reach and Frequency Data
Autor / Quelle: Yingxiang Zhang, Mike Wurm, Alexander Wakim, Eddie Li, Ying Liu, 2023, Google research white paper
Notiz: Extends the geo-hierarchical MMM to use reach and frequency instead of impressions, enabling optimal-frequency recommendations; this is the model inside Google Meridian (https://github.com/google/meridian, Apache-2.0, Python, verified).
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 or 3 reading for the Meridian lab. Free.

Titel: Packaging Up Media Mix Modeling: An Introduction to Robyn's Open-Source Approach
Autor / Quelle: Julian Runge, Igor Skokan, Gufeng Zhou, Koen Pauwels, 2024, arXiv 2403.14674 (Meta Marketing Science and academia), working paper
Notiz: The authoritative description of Robyn: ridge regression, evolutionary hyperparameter search, Prophet decomposition, calibration with experiments and budget allocation, and the organisational reasons for the design. Good contrast to the Bayesian school.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 reading (compare with Jin et al. 2017). Free.

Titel: PyMC-Marketing: Bayesian marketing analytics in Python (JOSS)
Autor / Quelle: PyMC Labs team, 2026 (year inferred from DOI series, unverified), Journal of Open Source Software, software paper
Notiz: The citable reference for the Python library the course will most likely use: adstock and saturation transforms, lift-test calibration, time-varying effects, multidimensional (geo) models and budget optimisation.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 lab citation. Free, open access.

Titel: Bayesian Time Varying Coefficient Model with Applications to Marketing Mix Modeling
Autor / Quelle: Edwin Ng, Zhishi Wang, Athena Dai (Uber), 2021, arXiv 2106.03322, working paper
Notiz: Lets channel effectiveness drift over time via kernel-weighted regression, which matters for multi-year series and for markets in transition; also the basis of Uber's Orbit library.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 background (time-varying effects). Free.

Titel: Hierarchical Marketing Mix Models with Sign Constraints
Autor / Quelle: Hao Chen, Minguang Zhang, Lanshan Han, Alvin Lim (Google), 2021, Journal of Applied Statistics (DOI 10.1080/02664763.2021.1946020 unverified); preprint arXiv 2008.12802
Notiz: Multi-region hierarchical MMM with sign constraints on media coefficients, estimated with a scalable algorithm; directly relevant to multi-country models where naive regression gives negative media effects.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 background. Free preprint.

Titel: Your MMM is Broken: Identification of Nonlinear and Time-varying Effects in Marketing Mix Models
Autor / Quelle: Ryan Dew, Nicolas Padilla, Anya Shchetkina (authors from memory, unverified), 2024, arXiv 2408.07678, working paper
Notiz: Academic critique showing that standard MMMs cannot separately identify nonlinearity (saturation) from time variation without extra structure; a useful counterweight to vendor enthusiasm.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 or 4 discussion reading for stronger students. Free.

Titel: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
Autor / Quelle: Brett R. Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava, Dan Chapsky, 2019, Marketing Science 38(2), 193 to 225, article
Notiz: Fifteen large Facebook experiments show that observational methods (matching, regression, last click) often miss true lift by a wide margin. The paper students should read before trusting any attribution or uncalibrated model.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 required reading. Paywalled, open PDF available.

Titel: Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement
Autor / Quelle: Brett R. Gordon, Robert Moakler, Florian Zettelmeyer, 2023, Marketing Science 42(4), 768 to 793, article
Notiz: Follow-up on 663 experiments: even with rich data, non-experimental estimates are frequently far off, which motivates calibrating MMM with lift tests.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading (pairs with Gordon et al. 2019). Paywalled.

Titel: TV Advertising Effectiveness and Profitability: Generalizable Results from 288 Brands
Autor / Quelle: Bradley T. Shapiro, Günter J. Hitsch, Anna E. Tuchman, 2021, Econometrica 89(4), 1855 to 1879, article
Notiz: Panel-based causal estimates of TV elasticities for 288 brands; median elasticity is small and marginal ROI is negative for most brands. A sobering benchmark for MMM ROI outputs and budget recommendations.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 reading (budget allocation reality check). Paywalled, open PDF available.

Titel: Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments
Autor / Quelle: Jon Vaver, Jim Koehler, 2011, Google research white paper
Notiz: The original geo-experiment design and geo-based regression (GBR) analysis; the template for every geo-lift test now used to calibrate MMMs.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 required reading before the geo-experiment lab. Free.

Titel: Estimating Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments in a Time-Based Regression Framework
Autor / Quelle: Jouni Kerman, Peng Wang, Jon Vaver, 2017, Google research white paper
Notiz: Time-based regression (TBR) for geo tests with few regions, estimating the cumulative causal effect from a counterfactual time series; the method behind many European geo tests where countries have few media regions.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading. Free.

Titel: Robust Causal Inference for Incremental Return on Ad Spend with Randomized Paired Geo Experiments
Autor / Quelle: Aiyou Chen, Timothy C. Au, 2022, Annals of Applied Statistics 16(1), article; preprint arXiv 1908.02922; Python package https://github.com/google/trimmed_match (verified)
Notiz: Trimmed Match estimator for paired geo experiments that is robust to outlier regions; with the companion design paper (Chen, Longfils, Remy 2021, arXiv 2105.07060, verified) it gives a complete, open workflow for iROAS experiments.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 lab (trimmed_match on synthetic data). Free preprint; journal version paywalled.

Titel: Inferring Causal Impact Using Bayesian Structural Time-Series Models
Autor / Quelle: Kay H. Brodersen, Fabian Gallusser, Jim Koehler, Nicolas Remy, Steven L. Scott, 2015, Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), 247 to 274, article; package https://github.com/google/CausalImpact (verified)
Notiz: The CausalImpact method: a Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual for a single treated market, widely used to read campaign launches and quasi-experiments in single countries.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 lab (tfcausalimpact in Python). Open access.

Titel: The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising
Autor / Quelle: Randall A. Lewis, Justin M. Rao, 2015, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130(4), 1941 to 1973, article
Notiz: Shows why even huge experiments are underpowered for advertising ROI: sales variance dwarfs plausible ad effects. Essential for teaching power analysis of geo tests and the limits of calibration.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading. Paywalled; working-paper versions circulate.

Titel: Attributing Conversions in a Multichannel Online Marketing Environment: An Empirical Model and a Field Experiment
Autor / Quelle: Hongshuang (Alice) Li, P. K. Kannan, 2014, Journal of Marketing Research 51(1), 40 to 56, article
Notiz: The reference academic multi-touch attribution model (consideration, visit, purchase stages with carryover and spillover), validated with a field experiment; shows how last-click misallocates credit.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 required reading. Paywalled.

Titel: Beyond the Last Touch: Attribution in Online Advertising
Autor / Quelle: Ron Berman, 2018, Marketing Science 37(5), 771 to 792, article
Notiz: Game-theoretic analysis of attribution rules showing how last-touch distorts publisher incentives and why Shapley-type rules behave better; the theory behind data-driven attribution products.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 reading. Paywalled; SSRN version available.

Titel: The Path to Purchase and Attribution Modeling: Introduction to Special Section
Autor / Quelle: P. K. Kannan, Werner Reinartz, Peter C. Verhoef, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 449 to 456, editorial article
Notiz: Concise map of attribution research and of the gap between user-level attribution and aggregate MMM; the whole IJRM special section (de Haan, Wiesel, Pauwels; Anderl et al.; Kireyev, Pauwels, Gupta) is worth assigning.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 overview reading. Paywalled.

Titel: The Effectiveness of Different Forms of Online Advertising for Purchase Conversion in a Multiple-Channel Attribution Framework
Autor / Quelle: Evert de Haan, Thorsten Wiesel, Koen Pauwels, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 491 to 507, article
Notiz: Uses a VAR-based, aggregate time-series approach to attribute conversions across online channels, which is in effect an MMM applied to attribution; shows content-integrated ads and search outperform banners.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 reading (bridge between MMM and attribution). Paywalled.

Titel: Mapping the Customer Journey: Lessons Learned from Graph-Based Online Attribution Modeling
Autor / Quelle: Eva Anderl, Ingo Becker, Florian von Wangenheim, Jan Hendrik Schumann, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 457 to 474, article
Notiz: Markov-graph attribution (removal effects) on real clickstream data from German firms; the method behind many "data-driven attribution" tools, written by authors at ETH Zurich and Passau.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 lab (Markov attribution in Python). Paywalled.

Autor / Quelle: Xuhui Shao, Lexin Li, 2011, Proceedings of KDD 2011, conference paper
Notiz: The first widely cited algorithmic MTA (bagged logistic regression and a simple probabilistic model); short and easy to implement in a lab.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 lab reference. Paywalled (ACM), author copies circulate.

Titel: Integrated Marketing Attribution: A Bayesian Framework for Privacy-Safe Granular Measurement Anchored in MMM
Autor / Quelle: authors not captured (unverified), 2026, arXiv 2606.16878, working paper
Notiz: One of the first papers to formalise "unified measurement": granular attribution constrained to reconcile with an MMM's channel totals, in a privacy-safe setting after cookie loss. Timely for the MMM-versus-attribution debate.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 5 discussion reading. Free.

Titel: Dynamic Marketing Budget Allocation Across Countries, Products, and Marketing Activities
Autor / Quelle: Marc Fischer, Sönke Albers, Nils Wagner, Monika Frie, 2011, Marketing Science 30(4), 568 to 585 (INFORMS Practice Prize winner), article
Notiz: The Bayer case: a decision-support model that allocates marketing budgets across countries, products and activities using response elasticities and dynamics, with a claimed profit improvement of about EUR 500 million. The single best academic match for the course's international allocation theme.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 required reading and case discussion; rebuild the allocation heuristic in Python. Paywalled.

Titel: Marketing Mix and Brand Sales in Global Markets: Examining the Contingent Role of Country-Market Characteristics
Autor / Quelle: S. Cem Bahadir, Sundar G. Bharadwaj, Rajendra K. Srivastava, 2015, Journal of International Business Studies 46(5), 596 to 619, article
Notiz: Hierarchical linear model across 14 emerging and developed markets: advertising and product innovation matter more in emerging markets, distribution and price differ by country type. Gives students priors for how elasticities shift across countries.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 reading (international angle). Paywalled.

Titel: A Global Perspective on the Marketing Mix across Time and Space
Autor / Quelle: Julian Wichmann, Abhinav Uppal, Amalesh Sharma, Marnik G. Dekimpe, 2022, International Journal of Research in Marketing 39(2), 502 to 521, article
Notiz: Reviews cross-country marketing-mix effectiveness research and sets a research agenda on heterogeneity across markets and over time; the most recent academic overview of the international MMM question.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 background reading. Paywalled.

Titel: Determinants of Advertising Effectiveness: The Development of an International Advertising Elasticity Database and a Meta-Analysis
Autor / Quelle: Sina Henningsen, Rebecca Heuke, Michel Clement, 2011, Business Research 4(2), 193 to 239, article (open access)
Notiz: Meta-analysis of advertising elasticities built on an explicitly international database (mean current-period elasticity 0.09) with country and method moderators; complements Sethuraman et al. 2011 and is free.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 or 3 (priors by country). Open access.

Titel: The Role of National Culture in Advertising's Sensitivity to Business Cycles: An Investigation Across Continents
Autor / Quelle: Barbara Deleersnyder, Marnik G. Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict E. M. Steenkamp, Peter S. H. Leeflang, 2009, Journal of Marketing Research 46(5), 623 to 636, article
Notiz: 37 countries over 25 years: advertising is procyclical, and the degree depends on national culture (uncertainty avoidance, long-term orientation). Shows why macro controls and country effects belong in a multi-market MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 background. Paywalled.

Titel: Price and Advertising Effectiveness over the Business Cycle
Autor / Quelle: Harald J. van Heerde, Maarten J. Gijsenberg, Marnik G. Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict E. M. Steenkamp, 2013, Journal of Marketing Research 50(2), 177 to 193, article
Notiz: Time-varying elasticities over 25 years show price sensitivity rises and advertising effectiveness falls in contractions; a concrete reason to model time-varying coefficients and macro conditions.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 4 reading (time-varying effects). Paywalled, open PDF available.

Titel: Financial Development and Country-Level Advertising Spending: The Moderating Role of Economic Development and National Culture
Autor / Quelle: Berrak Bahadir, S. Cem Bahadir, 2020, Journal of International Marketing 28(4), article
Notiz: Country-level panel on what drives advertising intensity across economies; useful context when students compare budgets and media prices across markets.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 background. Paywalled.

Titel: Open-Source Media and Marketing Mix Modeling: Practice-Oriented Overview, Challenges, Opportunities
Autor / Quelle: authors not captured from the blocked publisher page (unverified), 2026, Customer Needs and Solutions 13 (Springer), published 22 April 2026, review article, open access
Notiz: The first peer-reviewed comparison of Meridian, Robyn and PyMC-Marketing (LightweightMMM is noted as deprecated and archived in January 2026): Bayesian versus ridge-regression designs, who each package suits, and open challenges. Exactly the tool-selection reading the course needs.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 required reading before choosing the lab stack. Open access.

Titel: Optimizable and Implementable Aggregate Response Modeling for Marketing Decision Support
Autor / Quelle: Sönke Albers, 2012, International Journal of Research in Marketing 29(2), 111 to 122, article
Notiz: Argues that response models must be both optimisable (concave, interpretable elasticities) and implementable (simple enough for managers), and shows how to go from elasticities to allocation rules. The academic underpinning of the budget optimisers in Robyn and Meridian.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 3 required reading. Paywalled, SSRN copy available.

Titel: The Value of Empirical Generalizations in Marketing
Autor / Quelle: Dominique M. Hanssens, 2018, Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science 46, 6 to 8, editorial
Notiz: Three-page argument for using generalisations (elasticity ranges, carryover) as priors and sanity checks; a quick companion to the MSI book above.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 short reading. Paywalled; open PDF on the UCLA Anderson site (listed in search).

Titel: Marketing's Impact on Firm Value: Generalizations from a Meta-Analysis
Autor / Quelle: Alexander Edeling, Marc Fischer, 2016, Journal of Marketing Research 53(4), 515 to 534, article
Notiz: Meta-analysis linking advertising, brand and other marketing assets to firm value; provides the "so what" for MMM results at board level and a Cologne-based author who fits the DACH guest-speaker focus.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 or 3 background. Paywalled.

Titel: How Advertising Works: What Do We Really Know?
Autor / Quelle: Demetrios Vakratsas, Tim Ambler, 1999, Journal of Marketing 63(1), 26 to 43, review article
Notiz: Reviews 250 studies on advertising response and frameworks (hierarchy of effects, carryover, wear-out); the best short literature map before reading MMM papers.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 background. Paywalled.

Titel: Marvelous Advertising Returns? A Meta-Analysis of Advertising Elasticities in the Entertainment Industry
Autor / Quelle: authors not captured (unverified), 2022, Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, article
Notiz: Recent, industry-specific meta-analysis of advertising elasticities; a template for how students can derive sector priors for their own MMM.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 optional reading. Paywalled (check for Springer open access).

Titel: Marketing Mix Modeling Best Practices (Nielsen with Google and Meta)
Autor / Quelle: Nielsen, Google and Meta, 2022, report (PDF, about 20 pages)
Notiz: The most-cited vendor-neutral checklist for model specification: model at the most granular geography available, include non-marketing drivers (a media-only MMM overstated ad ROI by 68 per cent in Nielsen's comparison), handle digital granularity and reach. Companion Nielsen note analyses 19 Japanese models to show regional beats national data.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 2 (data and model specification) required reading; pairs with the geo-hierarchy lab. Free.

Titel: Modernizing MMM: Best Practices for Marketers (IAB)
Autor / Quelle: IAB (US) with MMM vendors, December 2025, report (PDF)
Notiz: Newest vendor-neutral industry guide; frames "timely, auditable, decision-ready" MMM, covers calibration with experiments, cadence, governance and includes cross-industry case studies.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 (measurement landscape) and Session 5 (from model to decision); free.

Autor / Quelle: Google / Think with Google, 2023 (updated 2024), report (PDF, 44 pages)
Notiz: Sets out the "measurement tripod" (attribution, incrementality experiments, MMM) and how to triangulate them; concise and well illustrated, so it works as a framing text for the whole course.
Verwendung im Kurs: Session 1 pre-reading; Session 5 for the triangulation discussion. Free.

Titel: The MMM Handbook: A Guide for Developing Impactful Marketing Mix Models (Google)
